title: Little Church
summary: Around 1844, the “ Little Church ” is built on the reservation. It was a Millerite Church, a branch of the 7th day Adventist Congregationalist church. The Millerites were part of the great revival from upstate NY. Today, there is little evidence of the church beyond photographs.
activity_update_summary: Consolidated the existing dated chronology into cited Historic Moments and removed the duplicate unformatted history block.
why_this_matters: Built on the Shinnecock reservation around 1844, the "Little Church" served a congregation of Millerites inspired by the intense religious revivals sweeping upstate New York. Although only photographs of the building survive today, the history of this chapel highlights how Native communities actively embraced new spiritual movements and adapted them into their own enduring social networks.
